blocks.text: Vascular disorders affect the blood vessels of the brain and spinal cord; examples are stroke and cerebral venous thrombosis.

blocks.caption: Stroke
rows: damage to brain cells when the blood supply to part of the brain is interrupted by a blocked or ruptured vessel
high blood pressure, smoking, diabetes, high cholesterol, obesity, family history of stroke

depend on the area affected: paralysis on the side opposite the cerebral infarction (dead tissue); aphasia (inability to express in words); sudden trouble seeing or walking; dizziness, loss of balance; severe headache

as soon as possible: medicines (blood thinners, clot-dissolving drugs, drugs for high blood pressure); surgery to remove a clot or repair a burst vessel; rehabilitation to recover physical and mental function

items: Ischaemic stroke: the brain's blood vessels become narrowed or blocked.
Haemorrhagic stroke: a blood vessel in the brain leaks or ruptures.
Transient ischaemic attack (mini-stroke): a temporary drop in blood supply to part of the brain, which may last as little as five minutes.

blocks.alt: Two outlines of the brain. Ischaemic stroke: a red artery blocked by a dark clot, with a dashed grey patch of tissue beyond it starved of blood. Haemorrhagic stroke: an artery with red blood leaking out into the brain. A note describes a transient ischaemic attack, a short drop in blood supply lasting as little as five minutes.

blocks.long_description: A stroke is damage to brain cells when the blood supply to part of the brain is interrupted. In an ischaemic stroke a vessel is narrowed or blocked; in a haemorrhagic stroke a vessel leaks or ruptures; a transient ischaemic attack (mini-stroke) is a temporary drop in supply. Causes include high blood pressure, smoking, diabetes, high cholesterol, obesity and family history. Paralysis appears on the side of the body opposite the damaged area.

blocks.prompt: A stroke in the left cerebral hemisphere paralyses which side of the body, and why?
blocks.explanation: The right side, because each hemisphere sends motor commands to the opposite side of the body.

items: Stroke: interrupted blood supply (ischaemic: blocked; haemorrhagic: burst; TIA: temporary). Risk: high blood pressure, smoking, diabetes. Treat fast: medicines, surgery, rehabilitation.
